Question: Is it possible for non-Catholics to attend mass with their Catholic friends or family members?
Answer: Attend, Yes. Worshipping in the pews and on the kneelers, Yes. Joining in taking a sacrament such as the Lord’s Supper, No. That is also the rule in most Baptist and some other Christ-based congregations. The reasoning is that visitors might not qualify in their beliefs or works to be righteous like them. Most Wesleyan churches like Methodist, Nazarene and others will allow visitors who believe themselves to be right with God, to share in the Communion meal.

Question: Why would a friend for whom you spent a lot of time and effort comforting when they had emotional problems show no interest in helping you when you are in need?
Answer: Is it possible that your time and effort comforting your friend isn’t equal to what you’re asking of your friend? I’ve seen a number of times that payback for some companionship and comforting is asked for in significant monetary terms. Your friend may not be able to help you now or may have failed to receive payback for a cash loan and be unable to donate to you what you ask. It can also mean that your friend simply isn’t as supportive as you are.

Question: Is it good that most people do not have social contact nowadays because they get to live like in the movie I Am Legend?
Answer: NO. Nobody really wants to live as the lone human in the world. That concept has been rehashed in “Robin (and Robinson) Crusoe,” ”Man Without a Country,” Tom Hanks in “Castaway,” and any number of science fiction stories long and short. Living without affirmation of one’s value to live, destroys one’s incentive to continue living. If you don’t believe that, go to a cheap nursing home and see what people who don’t receive that feedback endure. Why do Solitary Confinement and the Death Penalty rank as the ultimate punishments? It’s because they are declarations that the person is worthless of value to society.
